PRISM THIRD-PARTY LIBRARIES: SOURCE AND REPLACEMENT
=================================================

The included LGPL libraries are dynamically linked and replaceable. You may
modify or replace them, and reverse engineer the application as necessary to
debug modifications to those libraries. Application terms do not restrict these
LGPL rights. Keep a backup of the installation before changing runtime files.

SOURCE INCLUDED WITH THIS WINDOWS CANDIDATE

THIRD-PARTY/SOURCES contains the complete signed MSYS2 source packages for the
exact reviewed Qt, GLib, gettext/libintl and libiconv package versions. Each
archive includes upstream source archives, PKGBUILD build instructions, patches
and .SRCINFO. distribution-review.json identifies the source hashes and selected
runtime licenses; package folders contain the full license/copyright texts.
The MSYS2 packager public key and detached signatures are included. A network
source URL is provenance, not a substitute for these included source copies.

With GnuPG, import msys2-source-signing-key.asc into a keyring of your choice,
then run: gpg --verify <source-package>.sig <source-package>
The reviewed signer fingerprint is:
5F94 4B02 7F7F E209 1985 AA2E FA11 531A A0AA 7F57
Verify the SHA-256 values in distribution-review.json as well.

REBUILD ON WINDOWS

1. Install MSYS2 and open its UCRT64 shell. Use the x86_64 UCRT compiler family.
2. Extract a *.src.tar.zst archive into a new working directory using tar -xf.
3. Enter the contained mingw-w64-* directory. Read PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO; these
   record the source inputs, patches, configure flags and build dependencies.
4. Install the listed build prerequisites. Run:
      MINGW_ARCH=ucrt64 makepkg-mingw --syncdeps --log
   Verify source signatures using the maintainer keys listed by that recipe.
   Rebuild dependent Qt modules/plugins together if your changes alter their ABI.
5. Extract the resulting binary package into a temporary directory. Quit Prism.
   Replace the corresponding DLLs in the Prism installation, keeping matching
   plugin DLLs under plugins/ and QML plugin files under qml/ at the same relative
   paths. These files are ordinary replaceable files; Prism does not enforce
   the candidate manifest hashes at application startup.
6. Start prism.exe normally. --check-formats checks image plugins; --selftest
   runs development compatibility checks. Manifest verification tools report
   local modifications, which is expected after replacing a library.

The tested development compiler/package versions and runtime hashes are in
candidate-manifest.json and THIRD-PARTY/dependency-inventory.json. Different
compiler or library versions can require rebuilding their dependent modules.

TIFF

TIFF uses shared libtiff 4.7.2 with the optional JBIG codec disabled. The pinned
upstream archive, license and exact PowerShell build recipe are in tiff-runtime/.
Run that recipe from a Prism source checkout with MSYS2 UCRT64 to rebuild it.
TIFF with JBIG compression is unsupported. Other configured TIFF codecs remain.

OTHER TARGETS

This document and distribution-review.json describe the Windows UCRT64 payload.
macOS and Linux need their own native payload/source inventory and replacement
instructions before publication. A successful Windows review does not approve
those artifacts. No signed/notarized macOS or clean-machine claim is made here.
